pr_title: Add support to install collections from git repositories
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Fixes #61680

This adds support for installing collections from git repositories. Use the format git+URI,version (or git@URI,version to use ssh authentication) instead of a collection name. The version is optional and should be a git tree-ish instead of a collection artifact version. The version defaults to HEAD.

A repo can contain multiple or an individual collection. You can append #/path/to/collection/ to the URI to install collections from a particular directory in the repository.

This also adds a new `type` option for collection requirements files (which may be one of 'galaxy', 'file', 'url', or 'git' to override implicitly determining the type from the `name` field).
```
collections:
  - name: git@github.com:my_org/private_collections.git#/path/to/collection,devel
  - name: https://github.com/ansible-collections/amazon.aws.git
    type: git
    version: 8102847014fd6e7a3233df9ea998ef4677b99248
```

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Feature Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
ansible-galaxy

Does this support the `-g` flag like also for roles? (To keep the `.git` dir.)

@jamescassell No, it doesn't. .git directories are [not included](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/galaxy/collection.py#L869) in collection artifact build process and this PR installs collections from the built artifact data using the galaxy.yml file(s).
rebased again due to the test added in https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/69541

@s-hertel - I finally got time to fully test this and see if there were any weird edge cases, and I'm happy to report there didn't seem to be any. There were two things that tripped me up (though not directly related to this PR's changes): 1. For `role` installs, the `name` parameter reflects what will end up on the filesystem after an install, whereas for `collection` installs, the `name` can be one of galaxy namespace+collection name, or git path, or file tar.gz path (which is a little confusing coming from the roles perspective). For roles, the `src` was where you specified a filepath, git repo URL, or other source for the role. This is just a weird inconsistency between how collections and roles work, but since all collections _must_ be namespaced... I'm not sure if we can make any more consistency between roles/collections (roles don't have to be namespaced, something I like for playbook-local roles). 2. If a collection doesn't have a valid `version` explicitly listed in its `galaxy.yml` (many don't currently) then installation fails. Also a number of collections I tested with had dependencies that didn't exist, so those installs failed (would've happened even installing from galaxy!). Anyways, here's a test `requirements.yml` file I ended up with after testing a number of different permutations: ```yaml --- roles: # Install a role from Ansible Galaxy. - name: geerlingguy.java version: 1.9.7 # Install a role from GitHub, but specify a custom name for the local env. - name: homebrew src: https://github.com/geerlingguy/ansible-role-homebrew.git version: 3.1.0 collections: # Install a collection from Ansible Galaxy. - name: geerlingguy.php_roles version: 0.9.5 source: https://galaxy.ansible.com # Install a collection from Git. - name: https://github.com/ansible-collections/community.kubernetes.git type: git version: 0.10.0 # This doesn't work—depends on ansible.netcommon >=0.1.0 which doesn't exist. # - name: git+https://github.com/ansible-collections/community.crypto.git # version: 0.1.0 # This doesn't work—netcommon galaxy.yml doesn't contain a `version` key. # - name: git+https://github.com/ansible-collections/ansible.netcommon.git # version: 0.0.2 # Install from git+https (don't have to specify 'type'), at commit hash. - name: git+https://github.com/ansible-collections/community.zabbix.git version: b247fcf ``` I ended up with the following dir structure:

@geerlingguy Thanks for testing this.

> For role installs, the name parameter reflects what will end up on the filesystem after an install,

I thought about how this feature might work for collections if `src` was supported and `name` was allowed as a destination instead, but content in a collection could need to be edited to remain functional (some plugins refer to their own namespace, for example).

> If a collection doesn't have a valid version explicitly listed in its galaxy.yml (many don't currently) then installation fails.

Just to clarify, version is a [mandatory metadata key](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/devel/dev_guide/collections_galaxy_meta.html#collections-galaxy-meta) and it needs to be valid YAML, but it doesn't need to be compatible with semantic versioning until built+published. It could just be a variable, for instance.

> it doesn't need to be compatible with semantic versioning until built+published

Ah, perfect! So if you build your collection and use a placeholder in the git repository (e.g. `version: '{{ build_version_here }}'`), that should work?

It's the same requirement for `ansible-galaxy collection build`, the content of the key is only validated when attempting to publish (the server does the validation), the build doesn't care about the value, only that it's there and set.

issue_context.title: Support specifying collections in git repositories in requirements.yml
issue_context.body:
##### SUMMARY
When I **develop collections**, I like to store them in git repositories. Once they reach a stable point, I usually tag them and push them to Galaxy.

It would be a lot more convenient if `ansible-galaxy` CLI command would support specifying a **collection requirement in `requirements.yml`** that would **reference** any git "treeish" object (i.e. tag, branch, commit, ...) in a **git repository**.

---

Another use case is when a company creates some **private collections** for in-house use and **doesn't want** to deploy a **full Ansible Galaxy server** to be able to elegantly use them from a `requirements.yml` file.

Again, it would be a lot more convenient if `ansible-galaxy` CLI command would support specifying a **collection requirement in `requirements.yml`** that would **reference** any git "treeish" object (i.e. tag, branch, commit, ...) in a **private git repository**.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Feature Idea

##### COMPONENT NAME
ansible-galaxy CLI

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
The exact same thing is actually already supported when [specifying a role to install in the `requirements.yml` file](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/reference_appendices/galaxy.html#installing-multiple-roles-from-a-file).

I would suggest the same or similar syntax, e.g.:

```yaml
collections:
  - name: my_namespace.my_collection
    src: git@git.company.com:my_namespace/ansible-my-collection.git
    scm: git
    version: "1.2.3"
```

Like with roles, some keys could be omitted and the CLI would use some sensible defaults.

There might be some ambiguity between the `src` key and the [existing `source` key which is used to specify the Galaxy URL from which to pull the collection](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/devel/dev_guide/collections_tech_preview.html#install-multiple-collections-with-a-requirements-file). But it should be solvable and the details should be worked-out when preparing the implementation.

From [what I read](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/devel/dev_guide/collections_tech_preview.html#collection-versions), collections have a stricter requirement on the version than the old roles and require using Semantic Versioning. This again should be solvable since an appropriate version must be specified in the `galaxy.yml` in collection's root.

Set `name` as the URL, the source is designed to specify custom galaxy or Automation Hub servers.
oh ok, thanks. Now it works.. 👍

No worries name can be one of these three things

* The name of the collection, including the namespace, which is looked up on the configured Galaxy/AH servers
* The URL to a tar.gz which will be downloaded, unpacked, and finally verified as a valid collection before installing
* The path to a tar.gz on the local file system that does the same as above.

I've had great success hosting roles solely on internal git repos per-role, and avoided having to cut release tars, nor setting up an internal galaxy server.  The lack of the same capability helps make collections even less attractive...  Is it inherently difficult to copy the same logic from the roles processing to the collections processing, or to DRY it?

This has become much more frustrating lately, because there are _many_ situations where I want to install a collection from source (like I can do with Galaxy roles), but it's kind of a hacky dance that I have to do to be able to get it working.

```
mkdir -p ${HOME}/.ansible/collections/ansible_collections/community/kubernetes && curl -L https://github.com/ansible-collections/kubernetes/archive/master.tar.gz | tar --strip-components=1 -C ${HOME}/.ansible/collections/ansible_collections/community/kubernetes -xz
```

That's a lot more ugly (and almost impossible to remember, and requires extra tooling in some cases (e.g. Docker containers)) than something like:

```
ansible-galaxy collection install https://github.com/ansible-collections/kubernetes.git
```

Or something like that.

If the concern is that the installation is not as secure when you're installing from source or not from a signed Galaxy-style server, then a warning could be output in that case (or if the `requirements.yml` file references a repo instead of a Galaxy-style server).

Three cases that I'm bumping into frequently because of this feature gap:

  1. If someone merges some fix in a collection, but is waiting before tagging a new release (for whatever reason—laziness, plans, wanting another feature to drop, etc.), there is no way to start using that fix without hacking the collection into place (_and_ removing it from my `requirements.yml` file so Galaxy doesn't write over the manually-installed collection).
  1. If a collection is under development and is not yet ready for a release on Galaxy but is available on GitHub/GitLab/etc.
  1. If a collection is a private collection and someone doesn't want to publish it to Galaxy (this was a common use case for roles, and the idea was that since it's hard (or impossible?) to set up free/simple private Galaxy servers, posting the content to a Git repo was good enough.

I agree with all the things @geerlingguy mentioned.

I searched all over the other day trying to figure out how (if it's even possible) to run your own galaxy server and I'm sure someone's going to come along and post the link I missed but for the life of me I couldn't find any way to do it. 

I expected to at least find something on the galaxy site that addressed what is sure to be a common question, even if just to say "no you can't" and I gave up not being able to find an answer.

Besides that, I don't really want to run such a server; some team at my job is going to have to commit to owning it and maintaining it on top of everything else.

Being able to use our existing SCM as a source is the most useful way we could possibly make larger use of collections.

Given what we have already, I think without being to load from a git repo, we'd have to set up CI rebuild collections and publish a tar to artifactory and then load them with the URL syntax, making provisions for development branches and running tests and all that. It sounds very messy.
I will agree all things @geerlingguy mentioned too and I'm a bit surprised to discover different logic between roles and collections.

To @briantist's point above, I know there is the [Galaxy NextGen](https://github.com/ansible/galaxy_ng) project, which aims to make 'private galaxy' a lot easier (the current galaxy is not very easy to run or manage locally or on a VPS). But it is an order of magnitude more work and ongoing maintenance than the workflow users have been used with roles since 1.5.

Hello all, 

We are definitely looking at when we can get this functionality included.  It definitely is not in scope for 2.10, but if the stars align properly we will get in that version if we can.
@thaumos - It looks like it made it on the release train in time for 2.10 after all! 🎉
